header.note: September has 30 days and August 31, so every change is worked out on daily averages (period total / days). Search Console and Bing returned every day of both months. Google figures are the Search Console site https://www.example.com/.

headline: Key events (sign-ups, demo bookings and sales enquiries) rose 27.7% a day (949 in September vs 768 in August) while ad spend rose 21.2% a day, so the blended cost per result held at $39.71 vs $40.63.
LinkedIn's cost per result rose 34.0% to $75.15: daily spend up 42.8%, results up 6.6% (66 vs 64).
Google organic clicks rose 21.7% a day; the biggest single gain came from 'how to reduce no shows', which moved from position 8.4 to 3.1.
not_covered: Connected but not read by this report: the Facebook page, the Instagram profile and the LinkedIn page.

summary: September was a stronger month at the same cost. Sign-ups, demo bookings and sales enquiries reached 949, up 27.7% a day on August, while ad spend rose 21.2% a day, so each result from paid channels still cost about $40. Search did the most: Google clicks rose 21.7% a day, with the biggest single gain from the guide to reducing no-shows, which climbed to position 3.1. The one channel that got more expensive is LinkedIn, where each result cost $75.15 against $56.09 in August; the plan below holds its budget while we find out why.

channels.what_happened: $6,480 spent (+13.3% a day), 4,120 clicks and 318 conversions as Google Ads counts them (+25.4% a day), $20.38 each vs $22.56.
channels.why: Search | Online booking software carried 46.5% of the spend and 131 of the conversions. GA4 Paid Search key events rose from 197 to 238.

channels.what_happened: $4,960 spent vs $3,590 (+42.8% a day), 1,180 clicks (+34.7% a day), 66 results (52 website conversions and 14 lead-form leads) vs 64.
channels.why: The extra spend bought clicks, but they converted at 5.6% against 7.1% in August. Which campaigns took the extra budget is not visible in this account-level data; a campaign-level LinkedIn pull would show it.

channels.what_happened: $2,140 spent (+6.3% a day), 3,050 clicks and 142 conversions as TikTok counts them (+21.3% a day).
channels.why: The platforms' own counts run ahead of GA4: all of Paid Social (LinkedIn and TikTok together) brought 104 key events in GA4, while the two platforms claim 208.

channels.what_happened: 11,520 clicks over 30 days (384.0 a day vs 315.5), impressions +9.4% a day, average position 16.7 to 14.3, CTR 2.5% to 2.8%.
channels.why: 'how to reduce no shows' moved from position 8.4 to 3.1 and went from 5.8 to 20.3 clicks a day, 24.7% of the non-brand gain.
channels.brand_vs_nonbrand: The 1,000 query rows Search Console returned cover 71.1% of September clicks (August: 66.0%). Brand: 78.3 clicks a day vs 72.3 (+8.4%; 2,350 vs 2,240 in total). Non-brand: 194.7 vs 135.8 a day (+43.3%; 5,840 vs 4,210).

channels.what_happened: 840 clicks and 61,200 impressions over 30 days, vs 760 and 57,900 over 31 in August (+14.2% clicks a day).
channels.why: Bing moves with Google here; the run has no Bing query data to say which pages gained.

channels.what_happened: 22,400 sessions (+14.6% a day), 12,950 engaged, 949 key events: sign_up 734, book_demo 152, generate_lead 63.
channels.why: Organic Search grew most (7,240 to 8,610 sessions) and brought 262 key events, more than any other channel.

channels.what_happened: $4,610 from 94 'Subscription Started' conversions (campaigns $1,862, flows $2,748), vs $4,165 in August (+14.4% a day).
channels.why: Flows brought 59.6% of email revenue from 6,130 delivered emails, against 18,100 for campaigns.

idle_sources: None: every connected source of this business returned data in both months.
wins: Key events up 27.7% a day at a blended cost per result of $39.71 (August $40.63)
Non-brand Google clicks up 43.3% a day (135.8 to 194.7), 24.7% of that gain from the no-shows guide alone
Email revenue up 14.4% a day to $4,610, 59.6% of it from flows

issues.issue: LinkedIn cost per result up 34.0% to $75.15: clicks converted at 5.6% vs 7.1%
issues.fix: hold LinkedIn at August's daily spend and find the campaigns that took the extra budget (linkedin-ads-auditor if installed)

issues.issue: The ad platforms claim 1.54 times the paid key events GA4 records (526 vs 342)
issues.fix: judge budget moves on GA4 key events, not on the platforms' own counts (cross-channel-attribution-analyst if installed)

plan_next_month.item: Hold LinkedIn daily spend at August's level until its conversion rate recovers
